inevitable_need: A per-client record of exactly what our AI agents read, changed and were allowed to touch in each client's repos, kept separate per client, that I can export and hand to a client when they ask what an AI did to their code.
why_inevitable: Our clients' security questionnaires are already starting to ask whether we use AI on their code. Within a year one of them will make a log of agent activity on their repos a condition of the contract, and 'trust us' won't pass that.
must_have: Strict per-client isolation, so one client's code, logs and context never show up in another client's work
Data stays in our own cloud account or on our machines; nothing goes to a third party's servers
Close to zero upkeep: set it up in an afternoon and it keeps running without someone babysitting it
deal_breakers: A hosted service from a small vendor with no SOC 2 that reads our clients' Slack and GitHub
Needs someone to run and patch a multi-service Docker stack every week
Per-seat pricing that keeps climbing when we bring in contractors for a single client project
expected_provider: Most likely the AI tool makers or GitHub, built into the agents and repos we already pay for, because they already see every action and clients already trust them. A startup only wins if it's free to self-host and much better than what comes bundled.
memoryworks_would_need: The bit where agents report back what they did would have to become an exportable, per-client audit log that runs entirely in our own cloud with almost no upkeep, and the hosted version would need SOC 2 or a bring-your-own-cloud option. If it also briefed an agent on a past incident before it repeated during a two-week trial on one repo, I'd pay a flat team price.
